subproblem.title: Whitney ball cover of the complement with bounded overlap and local finiteness
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and let A ⊆ ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) be closed and nonempty. Write d(x) := Metric.infDist x A and r(x) := min{1, d(x)}/20. Then there exist a set J ⊆ ℝⁿ and N ∈ ℕ such that: (C1) J ⊆ ℝⁿ∖A; (C2) every x ∉ A has some s ∈ J with |x − s| ≤ 5r(s); (C3) for every x ∉ A, the set J(x) := {s ∈ J : |x − s| < 10r(s)} is finite and has at most N elements (Set.ncard J(x) ≤ N); (C4) for every x ∉ A, the set J'(x) := {s ∈ J : ∃ z ∈ ℝⁿ, |z − s| < 10r(s) and |z − x| < r(x)} is finite.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A : Set (Rn n)), IsClosed A → A.Nonempty → ∃ (J : Set (Rn n)) (N : ℕ), J ⊆ Aᶜ ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, ∃ s ∈ J, ‖x - s‖ ≤ 5 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20)) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, Set.Finite {s : Rn n | s ∈ J ∧ ‖x - s‖ < 10 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20)} ∧ Set.ncard {s : Rn n | s ∈ J ∧ ‖x - s‖ < 10 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20)} ≤ N) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, Set.Finite {s : Rn n | s ∈ J ∧ ∃ z : Rn n, ‖z - s‖ < 10 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20) ∧ ‖z - x‖ < min 1 (Metric.infDist x A) / 20})
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1-5 (facts (F1)-(F3)) of the parent-supplied proof of whitney_smooth_partition_of_unity (Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6, proof supplied after [EG92]), extracted as a stand-alone lemma. The parent's step 4 bounds the overlap twice: once by a measure comparison and once ("Equivalently") by a separated-set count. Here the separated-set version is written out in full, with the packing fact it uses, and it is also used for the finiteness of J'(x) (the parent's step 5).

Notation:
- ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), with Euclidean norm |·|.
- B(x,ρ) and B̄(x,ρ) are the open and closed balls.
- d(x) := Metric.infDist x A and r(x) := min{1, d(x)}/20.
- J(x) := {s ∈ J : |x − s| < 10r(s)}.
- J'(x) := {s ∈ J : ∃ z ∈ ℝⁿ, |z − s| < 10r(s) and |z − x| < r(x)}.

Claim. Let A ⊆ ℝⁿ be closed and nonempty. Then there are J ⊆ ℝⁿ and N ∈ ℕ such that:
- (C1) J ⊆ ℝⁿ∖A;
- (C2) every x ∉ A has some s ∈ J with |x − s| ≤ 5r(s);
- (C3) for every x ∉ A, J(x) is finite and #J(x) ≤ N;
- (C4) for every x ∉ A, J'(x) is finite.

Proof.

1. Distance and scale. A is closed and nonempty, so d(x) ≥ 0 and |d(x) − d(y)| ≤ |x − y| (lipschitz_infDist_pt). Also x ∉ A ⇔ d(x) > 0 (IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos). The map t ↦ min{1, t} is 1-Lipschitz, so:
   - 0 ≤ r(x) ≤ 1/20 for every x;
   - r(x) > 0 for every x ∉ A;
   - |r(x) − r(y)| ≤ |x − y|/20 for all x, y.

2. (F1) Comparable radii. Let x, s ∈ ℝⁿ with |x − s| ≤ 10r(s). Then |r(x) − r(s)| ≤ |x − s|/20 ≤ r(s)/2, so r(s)/2 ≤ r(x) ≤ 3r(s)/2. That is, (2/3)r(x) ≤ r(s) ≤ 2r(x).

3. Vitali selection; (C1) and (C2). Apply Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall with index set U := ℝⁿ∖A, centres x ↦ x, radii r, bound R := 1/20 (valid by step 1) and τ := 5 > 3. This gives J ⊆ ℝⁿ∖A such that:
   - the closed balls B̄(s, r(s)), s ∈ J, are pairwise disjoint;
   - every x ∉ A has some s ∈ J with B̄(x, r(x)) ⊆ B̄(s, 5r(s)).
   Since r(x) ≥ 0, x ∈ B̄(x, r(x)), hence |x − s| ≤ 5r(s). This gives (C1) and (C2). If A = ℝⁿ (in particular if n = 0), then U = ∅, J = ∅, and (C2)-(C4) hold vacuously.

4. Separation. If s, s' ∈ J and s ≠ s', then |s − s'| > r(s). Otherwise s' ∈ B̄(s, r(s)). Also s' ∈ B̄(s', r(s')) because r(s') ≥ 0. This contradicts the disjointness of B̄(s, r(s)) and B̄(s', r(s')).

5. Packing lemma. Let K ⊆ ℝⁿ be compact and δ > 0. Then there is N(K, δ) ∈ ℕ such that every S ⊆ K whose distinct points are at distance ≥ δ from each other is finite with #S ≤ N(K, δ). Proof: K is totally bounded, so there is a finite T ⊆ ℝⁿ with K ⊆ ⋃_{q∈T} B(q, δ/2) (Metric.totallyBounded_iff). For y ∈ S choose q(y) ∈ T with |y − q(y)| < δ/2. If q(y) = q(y'), then |y − y'| < δ, so y = y'. Thus y ↦ q(y) is an injection S → T. So S is finite and #S ≤ #T =: N(K, δ).

6. (F2) Uniform overlap bound; (C3). Let N := N(B̄(0, 20), 2/3) from step 5. It does not depend on x. Fix x ∉ A, so r(x) > 0 by step 1. Let f(c) := (c − x)/r(x); f is injective and |f(c) − f(c')| = |c − c'|/r(x).
   - Let s ∈ J(x). Since |x − s| < 10r(s), step 2 gives (2/3)r(x) ≤ r(s) ≤ 2r(x). Hence |f(s)| = |s − x|/r(x) < 10r(s)/r(x) ≤ 20.
   - For distinct s, s' ∈ J(x), step 4 gives |f(s) − f(s')| = |s − s'|/r(x) > r(s)/r(x) ≥ 2/3.
   So f(J(x)) is a subset of B̄(0, 20) whose distinct points are at distance ≥ 2/3. By step 5 it is finite with at most N elements. Since f is injective, J(x) is finite and #J(x) ≤ N.

7. (F3) Local finiteness; (C4). Fix x ∉ A, put ρ := r(x) > 0 and f(c) := (c − x)/ρ.
   - Let s ∈ J'(x), witnessed by z with |z − s| < 10r(s) and |z − x| < ρ. Step 2 at z gives (2/3)r(z) ≤ r(s) ≤ 2r(z). Step 1 gives |r(z) − ρ| ≤ |z − x|/20 < ρ/20, so (19/20)ρ < r(z) < (21/20)ρ.
   - Therefore r(s) > (2/3)(19/20)ρ > ρ/2 and r(s) < 2(21/20)ρ < 3ρ.
   - Hence |s − x| ≤ |s − z| + |z − x| < 10r(s) + ρ < 31ρ, so f(s) ∈ B̄(0, 31).
   - For distinct s, s' ∈ J'(x), step 4 gives |f(s) − f(s')| = |s − s'|/ρ > r(s)/ρ > 1/2.
   By step 5 (with K = B̄(0, 31) and δ = 1/2), f(J'(x)) is finite. Since f is injective, J'(x) is finite.

8. Conclusion. J and N satisfy (C1)-(C4). ∎

Remarks for formalization.
(i) The intended route is the packing argument of steps 5-7. A Lean proof of this exact statement along these lines was kernel-checked during decomposition. For information only, the parent's step 4 also compares Lebesgue measures: the balls B̄(s, r(s)), s ∈ J(x), are pairwise disjoint, lie in B̄(x, 22r(x)) and have radius ≥ (2/3)r(x), so #J(x) ≤ 33ⁿ, and similarly #J'(x) ≤ 68ⁿ.
(ii) Useful Mathlib names:
   - Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall;
   - Metric.totallyBounded_iff, isCompact_closedBall, IsCompact.totallyBounded;
   - lipschitz_infDist_pt, LipschitzWith.const_min, IsClosed.notMem_iff_infDist_pos;
   - Set.Finite.of_finite_image, Set.ncard_image_of_injective, Nat.card_le_card_of_injective.
(iii) The pinned SimonGMT file Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/WhitneyCover.lean implements the same argument in TotallyBounded.exists_uniform_separated_bound and exists_whitneyBallCover_overlap_bound. It uses r = min{1,d}/100 and the open-ball Vitali lemma with τ = 4. Adapt its source to the constants above. Do not import it: its prebuilt .olean files are stale for Lake.
proof_key_steps: Scale r = min{1,d}/20: 0 ≤ r ≤ 1/20, r > 0 off A, |r(x) − r(y)| ≤ |x − y|/20; comparable radii (F1): |x − s| ≤ 10r(s) ⇒ (2/3)r(x) ≤ r(s) ≤ 2r(x).

Vitali (closed balls, R = 1/20, τ = 5) on ℝⁿ∖A gives J ⊆ ℝⁿ∖A with pairwise disjoint B̄(s, r(s)) and, for every x ∉ A, some s ∈ J with |x − s| ≤ 5r(s); disjointness gives |s − s'| > r(s) for distinct s, s' ∈ J.
Packing lemma: a δ-separated subset of a fixed compact set injects into a finite δ/2-net, so it is finite with uniformly bounded cardinality.
Rescaling by r(x): J(x) maps injectively into a (2/3)-separated subset of B̄(0,20), giving the uniform bound N; J'(x) maps injectively into a (1/2)-separated subset of B̄(0,31), giving finiteness.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly states C1–C4 with every hypothesis. Vitali applies with bounded radii and τ = 5. Disjointness gives the required separation; the finite-net injection proves finiteness before bounding ncard. Rescaling into the fixed balls establishes both uniform overlap and local finiteness with valid constants. The proof is complete, non-circular, and supplies precisely the second child's cover hypotheses. The bare declaration name is unreserved.

subproblem.title: Smooth Whitney partition of unity from a bounded-overlap ball cover
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let A ⊆ ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) be closed and nonempty, write d(x) := Metric.infDist x A and r(x) := min{1, d(x)}/20, and let J ⊆ ℝⁿ and N ∈ ℕ satisfy: (H1) J ⊆ ℝⁿ∖A; (H2) every x ∉ A has some s ∈ J with |x − s| ≤ 5r(s); (H3) for every x ∉ A, J(x) := {s ∈ J : |x − s| < 10r(s)} is finite with at most N elements (Set.ncard ≤ N); (H4) for every x ∉ A, J'(x) := {s ∈ J : ∃ z ∈ ℝⁿ, |z − s| < 10r(s) and |z − x| < r(x)} is finite. Then there exist a type ι, functions φ_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ and points p_i ∈ ℝⁿ (i ∈ ι), and reals C ≥ 0, M ≥ 0 such that: (P1) p_i ∈ A for every i; (P2) every φ_i is C¹ at every x ∉ A; (P3) φ_i(x) ≥ 0 for every i and every x ∉ A; (P4) every x ∉ A has a finite set s ⊆ ι and a neighbourhood V of x with φ_i(y) = 0 for all i ∉ s and y ∈ V; (P5) Σᶠ_i φ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∉ A; (P6) for every i and x ∉ A, φ_i(x) ≠ 0 implies |x − p_i| ≤ C·d(x); (P7) for x ∉ A with d(x) ≤ 1, Σᶠ_i ‖Dφ_i(x)‖ ≤ M/d(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (A J : Set (Rn n)) (N : ℕ), IsClosed A → A.Nonempty → J ⊆ Aᶜ → (∀ x ∉ A, ∃ s ∈ J, ‖x - s‖ ≤ 5 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20)) → (∀ x ∉ A, Set.Finite {s : Rn n | s ∈ J ∧ ‖x - s‖ < 10 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20)} ∧ Set.ncard {s : Rn n | s ∈ J ∧ ‖x - s‖ < 10 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20)} ≤ N) → (∀ x ∉ A, Set.Finite {s : Rn n | s ∈ J ∧ ∃ z : Rn n, ‖z - s‖ < 10 * (min 1 (Metric.infDist s A) / 20) ∧ ‖z - x‖ < min 1 (Metric.infDist x A) / 20}) → ∃ (ι : Type) (φ : ι → Rn n → ℝ) (p : ι → Rn n) (C M : ℝ), 0 ≤ C ∧ 0 ≤ M ∧ (∀ i, p i ∈ A) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, ContDiffAt ℝ 1 (φ i) x) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, 0 ≤ φ i x) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, ∃ s : Finset ι, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 x, ∀ i ∉ s, ∀ y ∈ V, φ i y = 0) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, ∑ᶠ i, φ i x = 1) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ x ∉ A, φ i x ≠ 0 → ‖x - p i‖ ≤ C * Metric.infDist x A) ∧ (∀ x ∉ A, Metric.infDist x A ≤ 1 → ∑ᶠ i, ‖fderiv ℝ (φ i) x‖ ≤ M / Metric.infDist x A)
proof_key_steps: Distance facts and comparable radii (F1); J(x) ⊆ J'(x); nearest-point anchors a_s ∈ A with |x − a_s| < 3d(x) whenever |x − s| < 10r(s) (F4).

Rescaled ContDiffBump θ_s = θ((·−s)/r_s) with rIn = 5, rOut = 9: C^∞, 0 ≤ θ_s ≤ 1, = 1 on B̄(s,5r_s), = 0 off B(s,9r_s), ‖Dθ_s‖ ≤ Λ/r_s; vanishing (5a) near x when |x − s| ≥ 10r_s and (5b) on B(x₀,r(x₀)) for s ∉ J'(x₀).
Σ = Σᶠθ_s equals the finite sum over J'(x₀) on B(x₀,r(x₀)) (H4): C^∞ at x₀, Σ(x₀) ≥ 1 by the cover (H2), DΣ(x₀) = Σ_{J(x₀)} Dθ_s(x₀) and ‖DΣ(x₀)‖ ≤ (3/2)NΛ/r(x₀) by (H3).
ι = J, φ_s = θ_s/Σ, p_s = a_s, C = 3, M = 30ΛN(N+1); verify (P1)–(P7) via (5a)/(5b), finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset, the quotient-rule bound ‖Dφ_s‖ ≤ ‖Dθ_s‖ + ‖DΣ‖ and r = d/20 when d ≤ 1.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition includes H0–H4 and concludes the exact frozen parent contract. The proof correctly constructs nearest anchors, positive-radius bumps, locally finite normalizing sums, and the quotient family. Local vanishing justifies differentiation and finite derivative support; the estimates yield C = 3 and M = 30ΛN(N + 1). Subtype cardinalities, zero denominators outside the complement, and empty-complement cases are handled. No disjointness or parent theorem is assumed. Empty sibling dependencies are correct because the cover is an explicit hypothesis. The bare name is unreserved.
